title: National Quality Framework for early childhood education and care (all jurisdictions except WA)
summary: The Education and Care Services National Law and Regulations established the National Quality Framework, with national quality standards, ratings and phased ratio and qualification requirements, commencing 1 January 2012 everywhere except Western Australia.

instruments.title: Education and Care Services National Law Act 2010 (Vic)
instruments.provisions: Host jurisdiction for the applied national law

instruments.title: Education and Care Services National Regulations

commenced.what: NQF commenced in all states and territories except WA

direction_rationale: New national quality standards, staff ratios and qualification requirements raise compliance and staffing costs, which may deter small providers and favour larger operators (higher barriers), while quality ratings give parents more information.
comparison: Western Australia (commenced 1 Aug 2012, the next financial year); phased ratio dates by state
notes: Applied-law scheme across states (coded CTH for the national record); ratio/qualification phase-ins differ by state and year. Re-evaluated 18 October 2026 with monthly and quarterly data around WA's seven-month delay (docs/results_childcare_nqf_wa.md, pre-registered): no detectable early effect on childcare exits or child care prices; verdict inconclusive, grade Moderate.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: One national law for childcare quality: national standards, ratings, staff ratios and qualifications replaced separate state rules. Quality ratings help parents compare centres, but ratio and qualification rules raise the cost of opening and running a centre.

marks.reason: Adds assessment and rating, documentation and quality improvement planning for every service.
Higher staff ratios and qualification requirements raise the cost of opening a centre, weighing most on small providers.
Published quality ratings give parents information to compare services.
One national framework replaced separate state and territory licensing regimes.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on business entry or exit (grade Moderate).
